summary: Connect neural evidence to words or synthesized speech while preserving user control and exposing language-model assumptions.
outcomes: Separate neural decoding performance from gains due to language priors.
Design evaluation that includes unintended outputs, correction and natural conversation.
sequence: Follow intended communication to neural and acoustic representations
Compare phoneme, text and acoustic decoding
Introduce language priors and constrained vocabularies
Measure error, latency and conversational utility
Distinguish attempted and inner speech claims

visual.question: Did the neural evidence support this word, or did a language prior fill it in?
visual.interaction: Vary synthetic evidence strength and prior bias, including an out-of-vocabulary intent.

practice.task: Audit a fictional speech-BCI evaluation and correction flow.
practice.success: Reports neural-only and assisted conditions, vocabulary constraints and user-intent safeguards.
